# Durable memory retry receipts

The UI may finish a short host turn after saving a memory and lose its response. A retry must inspect the prior result before creating another turn. The existing operation hash includes turn context, so reproposing with a new turn is not an idempotent retry.

Add nullable `request_json` to the existing memory operation table, atomically stored alongside its hash/result by new proposals. This is the minimum evidence needed to establish original project/session ownership. `memory.findReceipt` validates stored request hash, original context and record, resulting scope, and the complete business request. It returns the original result without opening a workspace, writing a record, or requiring a live lease. Unknown fields are rejected. Claim whitespace is normalized with trim; ordered tags and supersedes remain significant. Old rows without the original request are explicitly unverifiable, not reusable and not recreated.

The portable archive envelope remains `craftmine.domain-backup/1`; exported schemaVersion becomes 2 because the exact memory operation columns change. Schema 1 remains accepted only with its exact original three columns. Verify its original hash first, then append null request_json in staging and in the atomic restore. Schema 2 requires the current exact columns. Unknown schema versions or mislabeled columns are rejected. Old backups retain memory content but cannot invent missing receipt ownership; new exports of restored old content use schema 2 with null evidence. The Windows native bridge remains format-neutral and keeps its 32 MiB limit.
